k-Fold Cross-Validation of a Fitted Model

Source: R/crossVal.R
crossVal.Rd

Estimates the out-of-sample performance of a fitted model by k-fold cross-validation. The data are split into k folds, the model is refitted on k - 1 of them with the specification of fit and evaluated on the fold left out, until every fold has served once as test set. The procedure can be repeated with new random splits.

Usage

crossVal(
  fit,
  data = NULL,
  k = 10,
  repeats = 1,
  folds = NULL,
  strata = TRUE,
  cutoff = 0.5,
  keepModels = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'CrossVal'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted with fitMod(), or a plain lm() or glm() (binomial, Poisson, quasi-Poisson or Gamma family), which is refitted through fitMod() with the matching engine. Binary models need a Bernoulli response (one 0/1, logical or two-level factor value per row); aggregated binomial data (cbind(successes, failures) or proportions with trial weights) are not supported.

data

the data frame to split. NULL (default) evaluates the data argument of the original call in the calling environment.

k

the number of folds, between 2 and the number of observations (leave-one-out). Default 10.

repeats

the number of times the cross-validation is repeated with a new random split. Default 1.

folds

an optional vector of length nrow(data) with predefined fold memberships, e.g. for grouped cross-validation where all observations of a cluster must fall into the same fold. Overrides k, repeats and strata.

strata

TRUE (default) stratifies the folds by the response for classification models and does not stratify regression models; FALSE never stratifies. A vector of length nrow(data), or a list of such vectors, gives the strata explicitly, see splitTrainTest().

cutoff

the probability threshold at or above which a binary prediction counts as positive, used for accuracy, sensitivity and specificity: a number in \([0, 1]\) (default 0.5), or "youden" or "closest.topleft" for the optimal cut-point of bestCut(), determined anew on every training fold (see Details).

keepModels

logical, whether to return the models fitted on the training folds. Default FALSE.

x

an object of class "CrossVal"

digits

the number of digits to print

...

further arguments, ignored

Value

An object of class "CrossVal", a list with the components

summary

a data frame with one row per measure and the columns apparent, cv, sd, min, max, nFolds (the number of folds with a value for the measure), pooled and optimism.

perFold

a data frame with one row per planned fold: rep, fold, nTrain, nTest, ok, error, for binary models cutoff, and the measures (NA for failed folds).

reps

a data frame with one row per repetition: rep, nPredicted and coverage, the share of observations with an out-of-fold prediction.

pred

the out-of-fold predictions as a data frame with rep, fold, row (row in data), obs and pred (the probability of the positive class, the predicted value, or for multiclass models the predicted class), for binary models followed by the cutoff it was classified with.

prob

for multiclass models a matrix of the predicted class probabilities, one column per class, its rows matching pred; else NULL.

foldId

an integer matrix of fold memberships, one column per repetition, rows matching the observations used.

coefs

a matrix of the coefficients per successful fold, matched by name and NA where a fold lacks a coefficient, if coef() returns a named numeric vector for every fold (unnamed vectors of equal length are bound by position), else NULL.

models

the models of the successful training folds if keepModels = TRUE, else NULL.

warnings, errors

data frames of the distinct messages and their count: for errors the number of failed folds, for warnings the number of evaluations (folds, apparent, pooled repetitions) that raised the message.

and the settings task, engine, formula, n, nDropped, k, repeats, stratified, cutoff (the number or method given), cutoffApparent (the cut-point of the apparent measures), levels and call.

Details

Observations. The rows entering the cross-validation are determined with the semantics of model.frame(): the subset of the original call is resolved with R's indexing rules (logical, positive, negative or row-name indices), and rows are dropped where any model term, including transformed ones such as log(x) or sqrt(x), the response or the weights evaluate to NA or NaN. This is done once before the split, so that the apparent and the cross-validated estimates rest on the same observations and the folds are of comparable size. A subset that selects a row more than once is rejected, as the copies could otherwise end up in training and test fold. Variables are evaluated on the whole data only to find these rows; every fold model recomputes its terms (e.g. poly() or scale()) from its own training data. Terms that cannot be evaluated on data are an error, as they would be for the original fit.

The response must be computed row by row (log(y) is fine), since it is compared with predictions of models whose response was computed on their training folds only. A response that depends on other observations is rejected if it calls a known data-dependent function such as scale(), mean() or rank(), or if its values recomputed on the odd rows, the even rows or the first half of the rows differ from those computed on all rows. The second check is a heuristic that may miss a user-defined transformation which happens to agree on that subset; such transformations are the user's responsibility. Computing the transformation in data beforehand gives all folds a common scale, but its estimation (e.g. of the mean and SD used by scale()) is then not part of the cross-validation.

Refitting. Each training fold is refitted from the call stored in fit with the data replaced, so the engine, family, link and tuning parameters are carried over. Row-wise arguments are aligned with the folds: prior weights, whether a column of data or a vector outside it, are evaluated once and split together with the data. Prior weights are used in refitting, but the performance measures are unweighted. An offset argument is not supported (specify it in the formula as offset()), nor is a formula variable of observation length that does not belong to data.

Measures. They depend on the task:

binary classification

auc (c-statistic), brier and brierScaled (Brier score and its scaled version, see DescToolsX::brierScore()), logLoss (mean negative log-likelihood), calIntercept (calibration-in-the-large: the intercept of a logistic regression of the outcome with the logit of the prediction as offset, i.e. with the slope fixed at 1), calSlope (the slope of the logistic regression of the outcome on the logit of the prediction). The two fits are separate. The intercept is NA if its fit does not converge; the slope is NA if the logits of the two classes do not overlap (complete or quasi-complete separation), if the logits are constant, or if its fit does not converge. Each case is reported in the warnings. The remaining measures are accuracy, sensitivity and specificity at cutoff. The second level of the response is the positive class.

multiclass classification

accuracy, kappa, brier (summed over the classes) and logLoss.

regression

rmse, mae, rSq (\(1 - SSE/SST\) on the test fold) and calSlope (slope of the observed on the predicted values).

Data-driven cutoff. With cutoff = "youden" (or "closest.topleft") the cut-point is part of the model and is cross-validated with it: every fold model determines its cut-point with bestCut() on its own training data and classifies the test fold with it, so the cut-point never sees the observations it classifies. The apparent measures use the cut-point of fit on all data, as bestCut(roc(fit)) returns it. A cut-point chosen on all data and then passed as a number would make the cross-validated accuracy, sensitivity and specificity optimistic. The cut-points are reported in perFold and pred; the pooled measures classify every prediction with the cut-point of its own fold. Ties of the criterion are resolved by the first cut-point that pROC reports.

Apparent, CV, pooled. Apparent is the performance of fit on the data it was fitted to and therefore optimistic. CV is the unweighted mean of the fold results over all folds (and repeats): every fold counts equally, whatever its size. sd, min and max describe the spread of the fold results; sd is not a standard error of the CV estimate. Pooled computes each measure once on all out-of-fold predictions of a repetition and averages over the repetitions. This is a different estimand from the fold mean, also for losses such as the RMSE, and the more stable choice for small folds. With leave-one-out, measures that need both classes or several observations (auc, brierScaled, the calibration measures, rSq, calSlope, kappa) exist only in their pooled version.

Optimism is the difference Apparent - CV: positive for measures where higher is better (auc, rSq, accuracy), negative for losses (brier, logLoss, rmse, mae). For the calibration measures it is merely the difference, without a better direction. For an unpenalised logistic model with an intercept, fitted by maximum likelihood without weights, the apparent calibration intercept and slope are 0 and 1 by construction; a cross-validated slope clearly below 1 is the signature of overfitting.

Cross-validation assesses the given model specification. A variable selection or tuning done beforehand on the full data is not part of the refit and therefore not validated.

Failures. Warnings raised while fitting the folds or computing the measures (e.g. fitted probabilities of 0 or 1) are collected and reported once, with the number of times each was raised (counting the folds, the apparent and the pooled evaluations). A fold whose model cannot be fitted, cannot predict its test data (e.g. because of a factor level absent from the training folds), returns predictions of the wrong shape or invalid values, or whose measures cannot be computed, is kept in perFold with ok = FALSE and its error, and is left out of the CV estimates; the function only fails if no fold succeeds. The pooled estimates use only repetitions in which every observation was predicted, as an incomplete repetition would describe a different population; without such a repetition they are NA.

For binary models, plotCalibration() and roc() accept the result and show the out-of-fold predictions, see rocTest() for comparing the cross-validated ROC curves of two models.

The split is drawn from R's global random number generator; call set.seed() before the function for reproducible results. Fit a model whose fitting draws random numbers itself (e.g. a random forest) before setting the seed: written as a call inside crossVal(), it is evaluated before the split and shifts the random stream, so that the folds no longer match those of another model cross-validated with the same seed. Survival models are not supported.

For mixed models, observations of clusters absent from the training folds (always so in grouped cross-validation by cluster) are predicted at population level, with the random effects set to zero.

The models kept with keepModels = TRUE support predict(), coef() and inspection. Their call refers to a temporary training set, so update() needs the data supplied again.

See also

Other data.split: splitTrainTest()

Examples

fit <- fitMod(admit ~ gre + gpa + rank, Admit, engine = "logit")

set.seed(1)
cv <- crossVal(fit)
cv
#> 
#> Cross-validation (10-fold, stratified)
#> 
#> Model:  admit ~ gre + gpa + rank  [logit]
#> Obs:    400, positive class "1", cutoff 0.5
#> 
#>              Apparent     CV     SD    Min    Max Pooled Optimism
#> auc             0.693  0.676  0.046  0.613  0.751  0.666    0.017
#> brier           0.195  0.200  0.013  0.183  0.216  0.200   -0.006
#> brierScaled     0.101  0.075  0.052  0.013  0.168  0.075    0.027
#> logLoss         0.573  0.588  0.030  0.546  0.626  0.588   -0.015
#> calIntercept    0.000  0.005  0.187 -0.306  0.312  0.004   -0.005
#> calSlope        1.000  0.952  0.391  0.528  1.717  0.835    0.048
#> accuracy        0.710  0.693  0.035  0.650  0.750  0.693    0.017
#> sensitivity     0.236  0.221  0.121  0.077  0.462  0.220    0.016
#> specificity     0.930  0.912  0.054  0.821  1.000  0.912    0.018
#> 

# the measures of every fold, and the variability of the coefficients
head(cv$perFold)
#>   rep fold nTrain nTest   ok error cutoff       auc     brier brierScaled
#> 1   1    1    360    40 TRUE  <NA>    0.5 0.6130952 0.2065777  0.01629690
#> 2   1    2    360    40 TRUE  <NA>    0.5 0.7321429 0.1839028  0.12427243
#> 3   1    3    360    40 TRUE  <NA>    0.5 0.7261905 0.1847553  0.12021268
#> 4   1    4    360    40 TRUE  <NA>    0.5 0.6495726 0.2113654  0.03651113
#> 5   1    5    360    40 TRUE  <NA>    0.5 0.6552707 0.2126330  0.03073291
#> 6   1    6    360    40 TRUE  <NA>    0.5 0.6581197 0.2051423  0.06487833
#>     logLoss calIntercept  calSlope accuracy sensitivity specificity
#> 1 0.6041265  -0.23602090 0.5810534    0.675  0.33333333   0.8214286
#> 2 0.5467780   0.05631846 1.7170110    0.700  0.08333333   0.9642857
#> 3 0.5499754  -0.06500459 1.0246174    0.700  0.25000000   0.8928571
#> 4 0.6192382   0.19016074 0.6309090    0.675  0.07692308   0.9629630
#> 5 0.6095431   0.05738940 0.7628065    0.650  0.07692308   0.9259259
#> 6 0.6011644   0.31168421 1.0474139    0.750  0.23076923   1.0000000
apply(cv$coefs, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
#>  (Intercept)          gre          gpa        rank2        rank3        rank4 
#> 0.4495185857 0.0004797699 0.1270814117 0.0869132107 0.1092291610 0.1643939428 

# the Youden cut-point, determined on every training fold
set.seed(1)
cvY <- crossVal(fit, cutoff = "youden")
cvY$cutoffApparent
#> [1] 0.3536984
summary(cvY$perFold$cutoff)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.2966  0.3528  0.3599  0.3573  0.3692  0.3912 

# repeated cross-validation, keeping the fold models
set.seed(1)
cv <- crossVal(fit, k = 5, repeats = 10, keepModels = TRUE)
round(cv$summary, 3)
#>              apparent    cv    sd    min   max nFolds pooled optimism
#> auc             0.693 0.671 0.055  0.533 0.782     50  0.667    0.022
#> brier           0.195 0.201 0.014  0.174 0.240     50  0.201   -0.006
#> brierScaled     0.101 0.073 0.064 -0.116 0.188     50  0.074    0.028
#> logLoss         0.573 0.589 0.034  0.526 0.695     50  0.589   -0.016
#> calIntercept    0.000 0.002 0.091 -0.188 0.193     50  0.001   -0.002
#> calSlope        1.000 0.909 0.373  0.099 1.751     50  0.818    0.091
#> accuracy        0.710 0.701 0.034  0.613 0.775     50  0.701    0.009
#> sensitivity     0.236 0.233 0.078  0.080 0.462     50  0.233    0.003
#> specificity     0.930 0.919 0.040  0.833 1.000     50  0.919    0.011

# grouped cross-validation: all rows of a cluster in the same fold
d <- Admit
d$id <- rep(1:100, each = 4)
ids <- unique(d$id)
grp <- splitTrainTest(ids, p = setNames(rep(1, 5), 1:5), output = "group")
cv <- crossVal(fit, data = d, folds = grp[match(d$id, ids)])

# regression
crossVal(fitMod(Fertility ~ ., swiss, engine = "lm"), k = 5)
#> 
#> Cross-validation (5-fold)
#> 
#> Model:  Fertility ~ Agriculture + Examination + Education + Catholic + Infant.Mortality  [lm]
#> Obs:    47
#> 
#>          Apparent     CV     SD    Min    Max Pooled Optimism
#> rmse        6.692  7.920  1.394  6.248  9.607  8.036   -1.228
#> mae         5.321  6.487  1.610  4.204  8.278  6.518   -1.166
#> rSq         0.707  0.445  0.208  0.187  0.730  0.577    0.262
#> calSlope    1.000  0.940  0.358  0.621  1.439  0.945    0.060
#>
